To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lead, when administered in small amounts to human subjects, is deposited in the skeleton and in the teeth; that the rate of absorption of the metal is proportional to the level of dosage, and is the same for the oral and the inhaled routes; that the amount of lead excreted in the urine is also proportional to the level and rate of absorption of lead, and that the rate of excretion is also the same for the two routes; that lead is excreted in faeces
lead, whether ingested or inhaled, behaves in the human organism as a mineral element and is handled as such.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behaviour of lead in the human body, and the effects of lead on the human body.
the behaviour of lead in the human organism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lead in nature, in its various chemical forms and physical states, is a ubiquitous constituent of the atmosphere, the water, and the soil.
, in man, the ingestion and inhalation of lead, as well as its excretion, are controlled by physiological mechanisms.
, in general, the body of a human being can tolerate the ingestion of lead in amounts which are not injurious to health, and that this tolerance is not impaired by age or by sex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have attempted, by means of the most accurate analytical methods available, to establish the quantitative relationships between the intake of lead by human beings and the output of lead in the urine and faeces.
we have been concerned with the biological significance of the presence and distribution of lead, in the body and in nature.
the lead in the organism is in a dynamic state of equilibrium between the blood, the tissues and the excretory products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lead is not a good thing.
the body can be exposed to lead in a variety of ways.
lead is a toxicant and that there is no safe level for lead exposure.
